topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Data Locality
explanation: Modern computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to bridge the performance gap between fast, expensive CPU registers and slow, cheap main memory.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of storage with varying speeds and capacities. Caching strategies aim to exploit data locality (temporal and spatial) to keep frequently accessed data in faster levels of the hierarchy, minimizing access time and improving overall system performance.  Effective caching is crucial for achieving high performance in computer systems.
